entries.title: Explaining an empty query result is linear in the conjunct count (one whole-filter probe past 64 conjuncts)

entries.notes: og storage.qnt guarantee B, mutant MS (conformance map GAP-1). Risk is held in riskHeld and retires only when a Published reply covers the current buffer version (bufferVersions moves on markDirty/addDirty; notePublished records the covered version), or the user replaced the buffer with disk bytes (noteBufferOnDisk), or the buffer left the working set. A title rename hands the risk to the new name, and the old record retires only after the new one is written. Threat: crash or power loss with the newer text only in memory. entries.notes: og storage.qnt mutant MX (conformance map GAP-3). keepAtSwitch snapshots synchronously (no await between it and resetStore, so no later edit slips past) and moves the snapshot into switchHeldDrafts, a window holder that releases a record only once its storeDraft resolves; loadGraphPath awaits it before the new graph's state is installed. entries.title: Editing a Markdown block keeps its hidden id::/collapsed:: lines in the block's own property group instead of moving them below the body, where Logseq ignores them (a block's id lost in Logseq breaks its references there)

coverage.failBefore:

owner:: Ada
body line
id:: ...'); on release/0.8 a vitest probe through splitProps/joinProps moved id:: below the body

entries.notes: Found 2026-10-24 by the data-safety review of the og property-hiding parity branch. join appended hidden lines below the body; with a visible property in the group (Title / id:: / owner:: / body) that made a second group, and OG's extract-blocks keeps only the first. Now hidden lines go to the end of the visible group (one group; OG's with-built-in-properties writes built-ins at its head, property.cljs:180, so an OG-layout block's rows reorder inside the group once); text without a group keeps the old placement (before a final quote, else below the body). The window's joinProps now delegates all Markdown placement to the kernel join. Bytes on disk were never lost in Tine; the harm is interop (OG, other Logseq-format readers).

entries.title: On macOS every CLI command that talks to the running app or tine serve fails with "the owner's endpoint failed: Invalid argument (os error 22)", because the owner closes each connection right after its hello
entries.notes: Darwin accept() gives the accepted socket the listener's O_NONBLOCK (Linux does not); the connection thread's first read returned WouldBlock and closed it; the CLI's next setsockopt on the closed socket returned EINVAL. Fix: make each accepted stream blocking. Diagnosis: tine-agents/specs/notes/gh771-macos-cli-einval.md.

entries.notes: Completes REG-WIN-WRITE-TARGET-TRANSIENT, which covered a page that cannot be opened. A page that can be opened while a rename replaces it can resolve to where the replaced file went (inferred mechanism: Windows POSIX-delete semantics move it under \$Extend\$Deleted), so containment compared unequal. A link-free entry that resolves under another name is now answered through its folder, unless it is a case variant in that same folder. Windows mechanism inferred from code and the CI failure, not reproduced on Windows by hand.

entries.notes: Reported by Martin on development: "Some page files couldn't be read: journals/2026_10_26.md: No such file or directory" while the file existed and loaded. A listed name absent at the metadata read is looked up once more: present means replaced (listed), absent means removed (skipped); the watcher delivers what arrives next. Syncthing versioning as the cause is inferred, not observed.
